'''Albert Kedrick Brown''' (born March 18, 1981) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and coach. Born and raised in [[Zachary, Louisiana]], Brown played [[college basketball]] at [[Okaloosa-Walton Community College]] (now [[Northwest Florida State College]]), where he was a first team [[National Junior College Athletic Association|NJCAA]] All-America selection as a sophomore.

Brown was drafted with the 11th overall pick in the [[2001 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]]. He was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in December 2003 and was later dealt to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in July 2004.

== Professional career ==

=== Boston Celtics (2001–2003) ===
Brown was drafted 11th overall by the [[Boston Celtics]] in the [[2001 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Complete Draft History : 2001|url=https://www.draftexpress.com/nba-mock-history/2001/all/all/|access-date=February 5, 2022|website=DraftExpress|archive-date=February 6, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220206033223/https://www.draftexpress.com/nba-mock-history/2001/all/all/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On October 30, 2001, he made his NBA debut, playing five minutes in a 108–89 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Boston Celtics vs Cleveland Cavaliers Oct 30, 2001 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0020100001|access-date=February 6, 2022|website=NBA}}</ref> On January 21, 2002, Brown scored a season-high 12 points, along with two rebounds and four steals, in a 106–97 win over the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Toronto Raptors vs Boston Celtics Jan 21, 2002 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0020100579|access-date=February 6, 2022|website=NBA}}</ref>

On January 18, 2003, Brown logged season-highs of 14 points and ten rebounds in a 97–95 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Boston Celtics vs Milwaukee Bucks Jan 18, 2003 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0020200570|access-date=February 6, 2022|website=NBA}}</ref>

On November 7, 2003, Brown scored a career-high 18 points, along with six rebounds and two steals, in a 87–94 loss to the [[New Jersey Nets]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=New Jersey Nets vs Boston Celtics Nov 7, 2003 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0020300066|access-date=February 6, 2022|website=NBA}}</ref> On December 13, he played his final game for the Celtics, logging two points and an assist during a 105–98 win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], the team he would be traded to.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Boston Celtics vs Cleveland Cavaliers Dec 13, 2003 Game Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0020300322|access-date=February 6, 2022|website=NBA}}</ref>

=== Cleveland Cavaliers (2003–2004) ===
On December 15, 2003, Brown was traded, along with [[Eric Williams (basketball, born 1972)|Eric Williams]] and [[Tony Battie]], to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in exchange for [[Ricky Davis]], [[Chris Mihm]], and [[Michael Stewart (basketball)|Michael Stewart]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cavs part with Davis in 3-for-3 trade|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=1686963|access-date=February 5, 2022|website=ESPN| date=15 December 2003 }}</ref>

=== Philadelphia 76ers (2004–2005) ===
On July 20, 2004, Brown was traded, along with [[Kevin Ollie]], to the Philadelphia 76ers in exchange for [[Eric Snow]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=76ers Send Snow To Cavs for Two|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/2004/07/21/76ers-send-snow-to-cavs-for-two/a99a6d30-cbf3-47e7-8f76-d79f177ca89d/|access-date=February 5, 2022|newspaper=The Washington Post}}</ref> Brown's final NBA game was played on February 4, 2005, in a 103–85 win over the Atlanta Hawks where Kedrick played for 2 and half minutes and scored 1 point.

=== Anaheim Arsenal (2007–2009) ===
Brown was selected ninth overall by the [[Anaheim Arsenal]] in the [[2007 NBA Development League draft|2007 NBA D-League draft]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=G League Annual Draft History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/draft/past_annual_drafts/2007|access-date=February 5, 2022|website=RealGM}}</ref>

Brown was selected 12th overall by the [[Maine Red Claws]] in the [[2009 NBA Development League expansion draft|2009 NBA D-League expansion draft]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kedrick Brown among Red Claws' picks|url=https://www.boston.com/sports/boston-celtics/2009/09/02/kedrick_brown_a/|access-date=February 5, 2022|website=Boston.com}}</ref> However, he never played a game for the team.

=== Bornova (2009–2010) ===
In 2009, Brown joined [[Bornova Belediyespor|Bornova]] for the team's first season in the [[Turkish Basketball First League]] (TBL).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kedrick Brown, Game by Game Stats (2009-2010)|url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/6875/kedrick-brown/games/2009|access-date=February 5, 2022|website=Proballers}}</ref>

=== Antalya (2011–2012) ===
For the final season of his professional basketball career, Brown joined [[Antalya Büyükşehir Belediyesi|Antalya]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kedrick Brown – Turkish Basketball Super League Player|url=https://www.tblstat.net/player/1567|website=TBLStat.net}}</ref>

== Coaching career ==
Brown joined the player personnel of the [[Southern Jaguars basketball|Southern Jaguars men's basketball team]] in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kedrick Brown - MEN'S BASKETBALL Coaches|url=https://gojagsports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/coaches/kedrick-brown/179|access-date=February 5, 2022|website=Southern University}}</ref>{{commons category}}
